taskPacket.objective: campaign close preserves every source the metrics and evals projectors read into docs/campaigns/<id>/ledger/ (R1).
instructions: Today preserveCampaignLedger (src/campaign/index.mjs) copies journal.jsonl, campaign.json and each linked run's usage.jsonl. Extend it so each linked run also contributes `<runId>.events.jsonl` (its events.jsonl), `<runId>.notify.jsonl` (its notify.jsonl) and `<runId>.nodes.json`: a projection of the run's node snapshots with exactly the fields projectMetrics reads. The campaign's `proposals/` directory, when it exists, is copied to `ledger/proposals/`.

The node-snapshot projection already exists: readRunNodes in src/campaign/metrics.mjs reduces a snapshot to {id, status, attempt, revisions, review}. Export it under a descriptive name and have the ledger write exactly what it returns, so the field list lives in one place. notify.jsonl is included because projectMetrics reads it too; the requirement title is every source the projectors read.

Preservation stays idempotent (running close's copy twice yields the same files). A run missing one of these files is skipped and named, never thrown: preserveCampaignLedger returns what it wrote and what it skipped (run id and source), and `faberun campaign close` prints the skipped sources.
No prompt, diff or worker output enters the ledger: the sources are exactly the files above.

Write the proof test in test/campaign/ledger.test.mjs, named exactly: a closed ledger carries every source the projectors read. It builds a campaign with two linked runs in a temporary FABERUN_HOME (see the existing tests in that file), one run missing notify.jsonl, closes it, and asserts every file above, the field list of the nodes projection, the proposals copy, idempotence of a second copy, and that the missing source is reported.

taskPacket.objective: projectMetrics reports intentToVerifiedSeconds and humanTouches (R5), and a run replace-contract substituted leaves every per-node rate, which publishes numerator, denominator and excluded run ids (R9).
instructions: R5: intentToVerifiedSeconds is the time between the campaign.initialized journal event and the event at which the last requirement declared by the campaign's phases gets an approved proof in the requirement closure; null while any declared requirement has no proof. humanTouches counts operator commands that changed campaign state after the first launch: campaign resolve, resume --answer, resume --reconcile, cancel, campaign add-contract. humanTouches is diagnostic with direction informative, never down (decision D4). The journal becomes a projector input; read it from the campaign directory and from the ledger (journal.jsonl) alike.

R9: a run that `campaign replace-contract` replaced (the campaign record already records the substitution; find where) leaves the denominator of nodesDoneRate and every per-node rate. Every rate publishes its numerator, denominator and the ids of the runs it excluded. A run canceled without replacement still counts.
Apply the same shape to the eval indicators in evals/metrics.mjs where they report per-node rates, so the evals rates also publish numerator, denominator and exclusions.

taskPacket.objective: Every usage record with costProvenance unknown carries unknownReason from a closed vocabulary, metrics reports the unknown fraction by reason, and campaign close prints it (R4).
instructions: appendUsageRecord (src/run/usage.mjs) writes costProvenance; when it is `unknown`, also write unknownReason, one of: no-usage-stream (the harness emits no counts: its adapter's capabilities say usage false), model-not-priced (tokens were counted but the model is not in the vendored pricing seed), provider-reported-nothing (the stream arrived with neither cost nor tokens), invocation-killed (the invocation ended by timeout, stall, cancel or signal before reporting). Decide the reason where the invocation's usage and pricing are resolved; keep the vocabulary in one exported constant.
Records written before this change have no unknownReason: readers treat them as `legacy`.
faberun metrics reports the unknown fraction split by reason (text and --json); `faberun campaign close` prints that fraction next to what it already prints.
If a usage-record validator or field registry exists (search for where usage.jsonl fields are validated or documented), update it too.
Write the proof test in test/run/pricing.test.mjs, named exactly: an unknown cost names its reason. Cover each of the four reasons and the legacy read.

taskPacket.objective: test/docs/docs-diet.test.mjs imposes one byte budget on SKILL.md plus references/*.md, fixed at the baseline's 46,855 bytes, raisable only with a new ADR the test finds cited (R8).
instructions: Keep every per-file ceiling as it is. Add a total ceiling of 46855 bytes over skills/faberun/SKILL.md plus every skills/faberun/references/*.md (measured at 46,852 on this tree after the previous campaign's cut).

The total may only rise with a new ADR: the constant's comment cites a docs/adr/NNNN-*.md path, and the test fails when the total ceiling exceeds 46855 unless the cited ADR file exists and is newer than 0010. Raising one file's ceiling without lowering another so that the sum passes the budget fails the suite.
Write the proof test in test/docs/docs-diet.test.mjs, named exactly: the skill and its references share one byte budget.
